headline.summary: Clear request path and good numbers. The scaling probe stayed shallow.

verdict.label: leaning_hire
verdict.rationale: Requirements and architecture meet the bar for mid level; trade-offs and failure handling need more depth.

competencies.name: Requirements and scoping
competencies.rationale: Asked for scale and read/write ratio, then used both to size the store.

competencies.name: High-level architecture
competencies.rationale: End-to-end path from client to store was complete and justified.

competencies.name: Depth and trade-offs
competencies.rationale: Named a cache but did not say what was traded for it.

competencies.name: Reliability and operations
competencies.rationale: Handled a cache node failure and a hot key.

evidence.speaker: user
evidence.quote: How many new links a day, and how many reads per write?

evidence.speaker: user
evidence.quote: The request hits the load balancer, then the shortener service, which checks Redis before the key value store.

evidence.speaker: user
evidence.quote: I'd just add more caching there.
evidence.note: No cost or consistency trade-off stated.

evidence.speaker: user
evidence.quote: If a cache node dies, reads fall through to the store, so I'd cap the miss rate with request coalescing.

strengths.title: Scoped with numbers
strengths.detail: You asked for volume and read/write ratio before drawing, and the numbers shaped the design.

strengths.title: Complete request path
strengths.detail: Every box on the sheet had a reason and the path from client to store was clear.

weaknesses.title: Trade-offs left implicit
weaknesses.detail: When asked what breaks at 10x, you added caching without naming its cost.

weakest_moment.question: What breaks first at 10x traffic?
weakest_moment.what_happened: You suggested more caching but did not name the bottleneck or the trade-off.
strong_answer_covers: Name the first bottleneck with a number
Pick one fix and say what it costs
Say how you would know it worked
weakest_moment.model_answer: At 10x we go from about 1,200 to 12,000 writes a second, so the key value store's write path breaks first. I'd shard it by the short code hash, which keeps lookups to one shard. The cost is resharding later, so I'd start with more shards than we need. I'd watch p99 write latency per shard to know it worked.

retry.prompt: Let's try that again. What breaks first at 10x traffic?

retries.note: Named the write path as the bottleneck and the cost of sharding.

next_drills.title: Short system design: rate limiter
next_drills.why: Practice naming the trade-off for each choice.

Links: Mobile app → LB, LB → Shortener, Shortener → Redis (read-through), Shortener → URL store.
tradeoffs_discussed: Cache in front of the store
